fields.v: Li, Q., Hu, S., Liu, H., Feng, X., Liu, S., Wan, G. (2026). MT-Web2Code: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Multi-Turn Regional Reconstruction and Localized Modification. arXiv:2608.03474v1 [cs.CV], 4 Aug 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2608.03474v1 [cs.CV]; no venue stated
Harbin Institute of Technology (Li, Liu, Feng); Meituan, Longcat Team (Li, Hu, Liu S., Wan); Peng Cheng Laboratory (Feng)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — MT-Web2Code benchmark of 102 multi-turn web UI tasks (16 domains) with Macro-Level Regional Reconstruction and Micro-Level Localized Modification, built by a Reverse-Corruption Trajectory Engine, scored by a dual-axis protocol (in-box fidelity, out-of-box preservation); 13 coding agents (LVLMs) compared

No SDD approach. 'Coding agents' are 13 LVLMs under one multi-turn interaction protocol, agent scaffold not described: Gemini-3.5-Flash, Kimi-K2.6, Claude-4.7-Opus, Qwen3.5-Plus, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro, GPT-5.4, GLM-5V-Turbo, Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Lite, Qwen3-VL-Plus, GLM-4.6V, Qwen3-VL-Flash. Kimi-K2.6 also used as corrupt agent and judge

N/A (no development approach). Per turn: current HTML, full-page screenshot with red bounding box(es), repair instruction ('Do not modify any other content on the page'), resource asset dictionary; macro level also a cropped golden reference image of the missing region

Construction: collect and render pages from 16 domains -> similarity filtering -> 102 golden pages -> element fingerprint injection -> corrupt agent removes semantic regions (macro) or injects 3 defects per turn from 9 operators (micro) -> reverse into repair trajectory. Evaluation: agent repairs from the fully corrupted state over 5 turns, each turn conditioned on its own previous output (chain), rendered and scored per turn
None in the agent loop. Author-side: manual check of generated micro-level instructions during task curation
N/A (no SDD approach run)
Not classifiable (authors do not use SDD terms)
Existing code base: iterative edits of an existing single web page (HTML/CSS) to reconstruct removed regions or repair localized defects
102 tasks: 53 macro-level pages x 5 turns (one region per turn) and 49 micro-level tasks x 5 turns with 3 modifications per turn; 16 vertical domains (6-8 pages each)

Front-end web UI (HTML/CSS) in 16 verticals: retail, multimedia, community, AI platform, CRM, ERP, public utility, government, HCM, TMS, publishing, news, vertical markets, procurement, knowledge, services
N/A (autonomous agents)
None

Macro: VLM-judge rubric scores (Layout, Elements, Text, Color, Spacing, Overall; five-band 1.0/0.75/0.5/0.25/0), S_inbox = mean of the six, S_outbox by block-wise VLM comparison with SSIM fallback. Micro: S_inbox = SSIM inside the repair footprint, S_outbox = SSIM outside plus colour pixel-difference penalty. Score = 0.8 S_inbox + 0.2 S_outbox; per-turn scores

Error snowballing: per-turn score gap between chain-based and independent (golden previous state) editing; caption ablation; judge cross-validation (mean difference, full-mark rate, correlation)
Automatic: macro by VLM judge (Kimi-K2.6) against golden crops; micro by deterministic pixel/SSIM alignment against golden renders; results averaged over three independent runs

fields.v: Tasks: 53 macro and 49 micro tasks, 5 turns each. Configurations: 13 LVLMs under the same multi-turn interaction protocol 'without additional task-specific optimization'; agent scaffold, model versions and settings not stated. Acceptance: golden pages as ground truth; macro judged by Kimi-K2.6 VLM rubric, micro by pixel alignment. Repetitions: three independent runs averaged. Ablations: caption vs no caption (3 models); chain vs independent editing (Kimi-K2.6). Human intervention: none

Macro: Gemini-3.5-Flash best (65.5), Kimi-K2.6 second (63.7); larger models such as Claude-4.7-Opus and Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview introduce unnecessary global layout changes. Micro: Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro best (83.5); most advanced models keep out-of-box preservation above 0.95 while in-box accuracy varies. Macro and micro rankings differ. Captions help Gemini-3.5-Flash (+6.3) but hurt Kimi-K2.6 (-4.5) and Claude-4.7-Opus (-4.4). Chain-based editing degrades with turns versus independent editing (Kimi-K2.6; accumulated gaps between +3.6 and +23.8 points across rounds, Figure 4, order not readable in the text layer). Judges: Gemini-3.5-Flash scores +12.1 higher than Kimi-K2.6 on average (corr. 0.91), Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview +6.7 (corr. 0.86). No significance tests

Per the authors, yes: the dual-track design separates structural reconstruction from fine-grained editing, and the chain vs independent setting isolates error propagation. Variance across the three runs not reported. Judge choice affects scores (cross-validation). Authors state no limitations of the comparison method

No limitations section. Gaps stated: agents struggle to reconstruct target regions while preserving surrounding content, lack fine-grained visual-code alignment, and suffer error snowballing over turns; strong static UI generation does not imply reliable iterative coding; deterministic metrics proposed as verifiable reward signals for training iterative UI coding agents

Values from Table 3 (p. 6), Tables 4-5 and Figure 4 (p. 7); Table 3 is partly garbled in the text layer (per-dimension cells of the top three macro rows hard to align; Scores confirmed by the text and Table 4). Inconsistencies: text says lightweight Gemini models outperform Claude-4.7-Opus, but Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite (58.8) is below Claude-4.7-Opus (63.0) on macro; Kimi-K2.6 is said to 'better align with human perception' but no human study is reported; Kimi-K2.6 is corrupt agent, difficulty filter, judge and evaluated model (marked * in micro). Thresholds (tau) and judge prompts not given. Code and data 'will soon be released' (not available). No pre-registration. Programming language: HTML/CSS
